gpt_3.5_turbo.note: Used for profile normalization, doc summarization

baseline_assumption.note: Conservative estimate for cost cap validation

profile_normalization.description: Normalize founder profile into structured summary

doc_summarization_per_chunk.description: Summarize one document chunk (800 tokens + prompt overhead)

final_plan_free_user.description: Generate strategic plan JSON (free tier, limited tokens)

final_plan_paid_user.description: Generate strategic plan JSON (paid tier, higher quality)

rectifier_if_needed.description: Single attempt to fix malformed JSON (rarely needed)

free_user.mitigation: Using actual OpenAI pricing (gpt-3.5-turbo), cost is $0.005 < $0.05 cap. With conservative baseline pricing, would exceed cap - mitigation applied: limit free users to 1 doc chunk max, use gpt-3.5-turbo only.
free_user.breakdown: Profile (400 tok) + 1 Doc (1200 tok) + Final Plan (1000 tok) + Rectifier (400 tok) = 3000 tokens max

paid_user.mitigation: None required. Even with conservative baseline pricing ($0.20), well under $1.00 cap.
paid_user.breakdown: Profile (400 tok) + 3 Docs (3600 tok) + Final Plan (2000 tok) + Rectifier (400 tok) = 6400 tokens max

notes: With actual OpenAI pricing (gpt-3.5-turbo + gpt-4o-mini), both tiers are well within budget.
Free user: $0.005 actual vs $0.05 cap (10% utilization)
Paid user: $0.008 actual vs $1.00 cap (0.8% utilization)
Conservative baseline pricing used for validation shows free users would need mitigation (1 doc max, no gpt-4), but actual pricing is safe.
Rule-based scoring saves $0.05-0.10 per user vs LLM-based scoring.

free_users: Limited to 1 document chunk max (vs 3 for paid)
Max final plan tokens: 600 (vs 1200 for paid)
Rule-based scoring eliminates separate LLM scoring call
paid_users: Uses gpt-4o-mini (cheaper than gpt-4o, 94% cheaper than gpt-4)
Rule-based scoring eliminates separate LLM scoring call
Single final LLM call (no iterative refinement)
both_tiers: Document summaries cached by SHA256 hash (eliminates duplicate processing)
Rectifier only called once if JSON parse fails (not iterative)
All token limits enforced via max_tokens parameter
Budget guards in worker code prevent runaway costs
